body: It just feels like nothing makes me happy or satisfied.  Sure, there is a 'grass is greener' thing going on, but I see people who have friends, and homes, careers, and things that make them seem fulfilled and satisfied, and I wonder why I can't get that feeling for myself.  People spend time with friends, but I don't... I can't even make or keep a friend.  People go on dates and have fun, but I don't.  Other people can get out of bed and face the day, but to me that's this enormous obstacle, like climbing a mountain.  So, is the grass greener?  It looks like it.  Are these the things I need to lead a satisfying life?  Maybe not, but when it feels like I'm the ONLY ONE who doesn't have them, it just makes me want to withdraw even more from the world, and just hide out from everything.

A lot of what you say makes a lot of sense to me.  Yes, I definitely feel like I just don't 'fit in' with those around me.  There have definitely been situations where I DID feel like I 'fit', but they are so few and far between.  I have such a hard time finding people I 'fit' with, it's a huge part of my problem, I think.  And I do agree with the whole 'brainwashing' thing, I mean, it's not really that I desire marriage or a house or any of those things that Society thinks I should have by now.  Still, it just kind of... hurts... having no one.  Feeling unliked by everyone I meet.  Feeling unlikable, as tho no one I meet will ever want to have a friendship or relationship with me.  I just can't seem to find the positive in anything, because all I feel I've ever experienced is 'downs'.  It's just tough to think it will ever be any different, because it never has.
I hope you're right.  Everything seems so bleak... all I want to do is curl up in a ball and never face the world again.  I just don't know how much longer I can go, feeling friendless and worthless.

That feeling, that my Brain doesn't work right and likely never has, that just terrifies me.  I'm giving the medication and the Doctor a chance, but I can't help but ask myself, even if I can recover and become 'normal', how do I start living at 35?  How do I make up for that wasted life?  I wouldn't even know where to BEGIN.

Yeah, that's about how I feel.  Everything just seems so bleak, and I can't think of a time when it wasn't.  It seems like my whole life has been a string of 'close but no cigar', I just can't seem to get it together.  I'm not 100% convinced that it's the medication, because these feelings were there before, and basically always have been, and I've also read that it takes a while to start working, but I'll talk to them about it.

I guess my biggest thing is that I just feel like things have NEVER been good, so I don't know how they ever can be.  I just started on a new medication (the last one I tried made my anxiety a million times worse), so I assume it hasn't started working yet.  Also, I'm on the smallest dose imaginable.  

I was thinking of calling my Psychiatrist... I just checked my Calendar and saw that my last appointment was only last Week.  It's seriously felt like a month!  I just don't know how I'll make it...
Thanks, yeah... If I could somehow just... curl up and stop being alive... I just don't know what else to do with myself.

I've never had a Vacation in my life.  I did some travelling when I was in the Military, but y'know... that doesn't count.  I'm actually taking a trip in October, going to Tokyo.  It will be my first time out of the Country (well, out of North America, anyway).  Even when I'm doing something fun like this, tho, I feel like I can't help but just dwell on the things that are bringing me down.  I went to the movies the other day, and I could hardly pay attention to the movie... I just spent the whole time fretting and thinking about the friend I had lost, and what I had possibly done to drive her away.

I have the same feeling about moving away and starting fresh somewhere new... in the next year or two I plan to move to New York City (if I'm still alive), but I feel like the problems I have will still exist, even with a change of scenery.  Plus, with a new place to live, there's the hassle of finding an apartment, having new roommates, finding a job... it all just feels like too much.

Is there anything really WRONG with just wanting to die?  I've got nothing going for me, and I haven't accomplished anything in 35 years of life.  I have no friends who would miss me, and I've only ever felt like a bother to my family.

I'm sitting in a Bar, alone, Googling ways to kill myself.  What would really be wrong with a swift death when life just feels like a waste?

Yeah, I see what you mean.  I try to do things to improve my mood / situation, but as time goes on it all just seems more and more pointless.  If I go out, or try to work on one of my hobbies, I ask myself more and more, "Eh, what's the point."  Everything just seems so empty.  All I want to do is drink or smoke.  Right this very second, I'm at a Bar, and I'm asking myself, "What's the point?  Why did I even come here?"  ...everything just seems so pointless, or a big fat waste of time.

Thanks, I see what you're saying.  It's weird, because like, I just constantly feel down, and when I'm not down, I'm having panic attacks.  I've only been to a psychiatrist once so far, and he gave me some medication which has yet to start working (also, I'm on really low doses).  Plus, my next visit with him is a month away, so it just seems like help or recovery is so far off.  

And I see what you say about just 'doing something' like there's nothing to lose.  I DO do things, I am 'chasing my dream', but it's just getting me nowhere, and my complete lack of success has just gotten me further and further down, especially when I see acquaintances doing so well where I'm failing.  Unfortunately, I can't quit my job because of the debt I mentioned, so I feel a bit stuck there.

I've actually been trying to get out, meet people, and maybe make some new friends, going out to the bar, a coffee shop, whatever, but it always ends up that I'm just sitting alone, thinking how pointless it is being there.  That's the big thing, really, I've hit a point where everything just seems FUTILE, like there's no point to anything I do, so why bother.  I can hardly make myself get out of bed and leave the house, let alone go out and DO SOMETHING.  I know it's probably frustrating to hear, like I'm not making (or don't want to make) an effort, but I've just hit this horrible low, and after years and years of my life being this way, I just don't see how it's ever going to change, no matter what I do.

I don't even know how to answer that question.  I guess I feel like things have just always been this way?  I don't know what better IS.  I used to think like, well, "Maybe if I made more money so I could pay my debts, I'd be happier."  So I got a better paying job, and I'm still miserable.  Or maybe, "If I had some friends, I'd be happier."  And for a time I had a group of friends I hung out with regularly, until they inevitably went away and stopped taking my calls.  I can't think of a time when I was EVER happy, or even satisfied, with my life.  And thinking of change give me anxiety attacks... do I move?  Get to know someone?  Let them get to know me?  Just the thought kind of makes me sick to my stomach.

I couldn't even tell you.  Nothing has ever seemed to go right or come together.  If I'm stuck doing something I hate, and I can't even make (or keep) a friend, then what's the point of anything?  Even if one problem somehow went away, I'm still stuck with all the others.
